newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-NatFoods eyes Asia for growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-NatFoods eyes Asia for growth.

text.p: Food group National Foods Ltd will look to Asia for long-term growth, managing director Max Ould said on Tuesday after announcing a net loss of A$12.31 million for the six months to December 31.
Ould said National Foods would focus on its milk and dairy foods divisions for growth in the short-term, which should bring a strong improvement in full year earnings.
But the company had to look internationally further out. "We must find a bridge into Asia," he told a media briefing.
National Foods' half year loss came after booking after tax abnormals of A$25.7 million, related to a restructuring.
Ould said the milk group put in a creditable peformance while dairy foods were stronger, but the juice group remained a problem.
Juice sales fell four percent to A$77 million and earnings before interest and tax slipped 60 percent to just A$0.9 million.
Ould said he was looking to reduce fixed costs in the juice business and would probably eliminate some existing brands.
Ould said he would be disappointed if National Foods had not replaced the earnings stream of NationalPak, sold in February for A$206 million, within 12-18 months.
"Any investments we make in future will underpin our core business," he said.
However, the group also had to invest for a future in Asia.
He expected that within three-to-five years, 10-15 percent of the group's earnings would come from new businesses, most likely offshore.
Ould said the Yoplait licence could be available in Asia, but noted that Asian markets remained small and fragmented in terms of diary product and juice consumption.
Australia had per capita milk consumption of 106 litres of milk a year, compared with 11 litres in Hong Kong and two litres in Thailand.
However, he added that Asia's total beverage market of 2.5 billion litres, about the same of Australia's, was expected to rise to 4.5 billion litres by 2001.
"So the growth is rapid and we had better be on the ground there," he said.
Ould said National Foods would consider outsourcing some of its transport operations to free-up capital.
Farm pick-up and distribution from processing to depots, were operated in-house and tied up A$15-A$17 million in assets.
"If someone were to buy them and provide the services at a lower cost I think I would be fairly encouraged to do that," he said.
Ould also said he did not expect any further large abnormals in the second half, and denied the group was a takeover target.
"No-one has approached us and we have heard no rumours of any potential concern and to my knowledge our Asian shareholders are comfortable with the direction we are taking," he said.
Mingly Corp holds about 10.4 percent of National Foods and Singapore group Camerlin Pte Ltd about eight percent.
National Foods shares ended one cent lower at A$1.49 on Tuesday.
-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
